title: "Tasmanian places"
subtitle: "A knowledge base of places, built from open data and sourced history"

---

This site collects what open data and published sources say about places in Tasmania, one place at a time. It started with a simple question: *what can theLIST tell me about a property?*

## How it is organised

**[Places](places/index.qmd)** are the hub. A place is a property in theLIST cadastre. Each place page holds its extracted facts (titles, area, buildings, zones, fire history, elevation, rivers, heritage entries), its sourced history, a map, and links to connected places.

**Themes** are reasons for asking. A report is written for one theme and links back to its places:

- **[Properties](properties/index.qmd)**: what and where a property is, its history and structures, and why it is hard to find on theLIST.
- **[Geotech](geotech/index.qmd)**: desk-study packs for a site visit, covering ground, water, hazards, services and contamination history.

More themes can be added as questions arise, for example climate and weather records, or what satellite imagery shows over time.

## How it grows

Places are worked through from a [ranked queue](places/index.qmd#next-in-the-queue): larger properties first, with a bias towards those closer to Hobart. Anyone can [request a place](request.qmd) or add a question about one.

As places are added they link to each other through shared rivers, boundaries, fires and named features, and later through people and events in their histories.

## What it is not

It is not an authoritative record. theLIST, Heritage Tasmania and the archives are. See [About](about.qmd) for the rules on sources, people and sensitive history.
